findings.subject: 1900 electric tram to Tacubaya
findings.assertion: Mario Camarena describes the 1900 inauguration of an electric tram line serving Tacubaya, linking the old core of Mexico City with western settlements; the same abstract discusses drainage and lighting changes.
findings.remaining_uncertainty: Specific route schedule, operators, exact inauguration day not independently examined
findings.suggested_educational_use: Place-based chronological narrative or optional evidence caveat

findings.subject: Tlalpan animal-drawn and electric trams
findings.assertion: INAH dates the start of animal-drawn tram service in Tlalpan to 1891 and describes a 1900 electric tram connection from the Zócalo to San Fernando.
findings.remaining_uncertainty: Contemporary schedules not examined; connection may involve more than one operational stage
findings.suggested_educational_use: Place-based chronological narrative or optional evidence caveat

findings.subject: Urban growth from 1858 to 1910
findings.assertion: UNAM CCH's teaching material reports an area of 8.5 square kilometres for Mexico City in 1858 and 40.5 in 1910; their underlying boundary and measurement definitions have not yet been validated.
findings.remaining_uncertainty: Do not publish the two numbers until definition of urban area and source series are checked
findings.suggested_educational_use: Place-based chronological narrative or optional evidence caveat

findings.subject: February 1913 coup in Mexico City
findings.assertion: INEHRM describes the Decena Trágica as the February 9–23, 1913 Mexico City upheaval in which Victoriano Huerta's military coup overthrew President Francisco I. Madero and Vice President José María Pino Suárez.
evidence_locators: INEHRM Revolution catalogue, La Decena Trágica synopsis
findings.remaining_uncertainty: Detailed daily chronology and military geography require primary-source scrutiny
findings.suggested_educational_use: Place-based chronological narrative or optional evidence caveat

findings.subject: San Francisco convent 1861 closure
findings.assertion: INAH describes the main San Francisco church's 1861 closure, dismantling of some altarpieces, tribunes and choir furnishings, transfer of paintings to the Academy of Fine Arts, and destruction or division of convent spaces.
findings.remaining_uncertainty: Potential duplicate of stg-20261112-reforma-11; requires enrichment mapping rather than double teaching
findings.suggested_educational_use: Place-based chronological narrative or optional evidence caveat

findings.subject: San Francisco later ownership history
findings.assertion: The INAH monument catalogue describes the post-Reform transfer of the San Francisco church to an Episcopal Protestant congregation, its sale to the Jesuits on June 21, 1898, and Franciscan return around 1948.
evidence_locators: INAH monument catalogue entry 11735, later institutional ownership
findings.remaining_uncertainty: Property deeds and building-by-building ownership not independently examined
findings.suggested_educational_use: Place-based chronological narrative or optional evidence caveat

findings.subject: Tlatelolco reconstruction and tenure
findings.assertion: An official reconstruction directive reproduced in a UNAM-published 1986 documentary abstract states that reconstruction work at the Nonoalco-Tlatelolco housing complex would not be conditional on changes to residents' existing property regime.
evidence_locators: Revista Mexicana de Sociología 48(2), documentary excerpt in published abstract, directives 1 and 3
findings.remaining_uncertainty: Prescribed government policy, not proof of implementation
findings.suggested_educational_use: Place-based chronological narrative or optional evidence caveat

findings.subject: Tlatelolco reconstruction financing
findings.assertion: The same official Tlatelolco reconstruction directive envisaged paying rebuilding costs from insurance proceeds and congressionally approved reconstruction resources.
evidence_locators: Revista Mexicana de Sociología 48(2), documentary excerpt in published abstract, directive 2
findings.remaining_uncertainty: Insurance settlements, real expenditures and resident charges not verified
findings.suggested_educational_use: Place-based chronological narrative or optional evidence caveat

findings.subject: Incomparable estimates of 1985 housing damage
findings.assertion: Rabell and Mier y Terán's 1986 abstract juxtaposes 3,745 damaged residential buildings, about 90,000 affected dwellings (30,000 requiring demolition), and 46,000 families needing assistance from different agencies; these refer to different units and measurement scopes.
evidence_locators: Rabell and Mier y Terán (1986), abstract paragraph on damage estimates
findings.remaining_uncertainty: Original government counts, survey definitions and uncertainty ranges not checked
findings.suggested_educational_use: Place-based chronological narrative or optional evidence caveat

findings.subject: Post-quake garment workers
findings.assertion: Lucía Álvarez Mosso's December 1985 abstract describes low wages, long hours and intense production demands in garment work, and discusses workplace closures and insecure employment after the September earthquakes.
evidence_locators: UNAM IIEc, Momento Económico (21), abstract; article pp.14–15 not read
findings.remaining_uncertainty: Factory payrolls and survivor testimony needed before quantification
findings.suggested_educational_use: Place-based chronological narrative or optional evidence caveat

findings.subject: Collective memory of the 1985 and 2017 earthquakes
findings.assertion: In a 2018 journal abstract, Eugenia Allier Montaño reports that the September 2017 national press frequently compared the 2017 earthquake with 1985, discussing rescue volunteers, affected areas and government actions.
evidence_locators: Allier Montaño (2018), journal abstract on newspaper analysis
findings.remaining_uncertainty: Full news corpus not independently inspected; findings concern published press discussion, not all residents
findings.suggested_educational_use: Place-based chronological narrative or optional evidence caveat
